newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU must fund food aid not nuclear plant - Euro-MPs.
newsitem.headline: EU must fund food aid not nuclear plant - Euro-MPs.

text.p: Euro-MPs slammed European Union governments on Tuesday for planning to pour money into North Korea's nuclear industry, saying the money should be used instead to stem the famine sweeping the country.

The 15 EU states agreed in 1995 to grant 75 million Ecus over five years towards a five-billion-dollar international project also involving the United States, Canada and Japan to build two light water reactors at North Korea's Kedo plant.

Five million Ecus have already been granted this year but the European Commission is expected to ask the European Parliament -- which shares control over the budget with the Council of Ministers -- to approve the release of a further 10 million.
Detlev Samland, the German Socialist head of parliament's budget committee, told a news conference Euro-MPs were likely to reject the request.

German Green Euro-MP Undine von Blottnitz said the EU contribution was an "entrance fee" which allowed Europe to muscle in on a 2000 megawatt commercial project which would otherwise be controlled by its competitors.
In the meantime, North Koreans had been reduced to eating grass and bark to stave off starvation and the EU was saying it did not have adequate money for food aid, she told reporters.
Samland said he would urge EU Humanitarian Commissioner Emma Bonino on Wednesday to fight for the 10 million Ecu package to be spent on food aid, not the nuclear plant.
The European Parliament is due on Thursday to adopt a resolution on the EU's policy towards the crisis in North Korea.
